title: The game the internet made young again
text: {{1}} was the pandemic that revived chess. Although chess is {{2}} of the world's oldest games, it had spent decades quietly fading in the West, its clubs greying {{3}} its fixtures thinning, until lockdown handed it perfect conditions: housebound players, a streaming boom and a generation looking {{4}} something to argue about. The Queen's Gambit, a drama {{5}} heroine journeys from orphanage to grandmaster, became the platform's most-watched scripted series, {{6}} sales of chess sets soared. The game's largest website reported that {{7}} of its millions of newcomers were young, casual and — to the old guard's surprise — increasingly female. The old game has not changed; {{8}} has changed is who is playing it.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ was the pandemic that
gaps.explanation: The cleft structure emphasises the pandemic.

gaps.hint: pronoun: chess is ___ of the world's oldest games
gaps.explanation: 'One of the + superlative' — the standard pattern.
The two absolute phrases are joined by 'and'.

gaps.hint: preposition: looking ___ something to argue about

gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the drama to its heroine.

gaps.hint: conjunction: series, ___ sales of sets soared
gaps.explanation: The two results are added: and.

gaps.hint: quantifier: ___ of its millions of newcomers
gaps.explanation: 'Most of' — the majority of the newcomers.

gaps.hint: pronoun: ___ has changed is who is playing
gaps.explanation: Fused relative subject: what has changed.
